title: Synthetic Factory Tag Taxonomy v1
description: A compact controlled vocabulary for curated corpus tags. Every canonical tag is 'facet:term'. A source tag becomes canonical only through an alias declared here or an anchored pattern rule declared here. Anything else stays unmapped: it is dropped from the curated tag list, reported explicitly, and preserved verbatim in the record's tag_provenance so the original vocabulary remains recoverable. The taxonomy never guesses at the meaning of a one-off label.

normalization.description: Alias and pattern lookup happens on the normalized form of a source tag, so case and separator variants fold together without a separate alias entry. Normalization is a lexical fold only; it never assigns meaning.
steps: replace every run of characters outside [a-z0-9] with a single underscore

facets.description: What the tagged record is. Only record kinds that the 2026-08-17 corpus actually names in its own tags appear here.

terms.definition: The record is a chosen/rejected preference pair.
The record is a thalamic trajectory.
The record carries a spike raster excerpt rather than a full raster.

facets.description: The safety-gate decision named by the tag. Only the bare decision words map here. Compound labels such as 'wrong_REJECT', 'ACCEPT_defective', or 'REJECT_with_replan' judge or qualify a decision rather than name one, so they stay unmapped instead of being folded into a decision term.

terms.definition: The tag names an ACCEPT gate decision.
The tag names a MODIFY gate decision.
The tag names a REJECT gate decision.

facets.description: Which side of a preference pair the tagged container belongs to.

terms.definition: The container belongs to the chosen side of a preference pair.
The container belongs to the rejected side of a preference pair.

facets.description: The shape of the reward signal the tag describes. These terms describe shape only and say nothing about magnitude comparability, which reward ontology v1 owns.

terms.definition: Reward is emitted per simulation tick.
Reward is emitted on sparse ticks rather than every tick.
The record's total reward is negative.

facets.description: How a preference pair was constructed.

terms.definition: The two sides share a byte-identical context and differ only in the gate decision.
The two sides share a context and differ in gate memory, so the pair teaches gate learning.
The two sides are close enough that the pair is a near miss. Intensity qualifiers on the source label, such as 'nuanced', are dropped here and remain recoverable in tag_provenance.

facets.description: How the tagged scenario came to exist. This facet mirrors schemas/provenance.md and never asserts that a scenario was measured.

terms.definition: The plant in the record was designed rather than measured.

facets.description: Release readiness the source corpus claimed for the record.

terms.definition: The source corpus marked the record ready for distillation. The tag records the claim; it is not an audit result.

facets.description: Generation-process bookkeeping carried in tags. Terms in this facet are reached through pattern rules because the source labels embed a pass number or a round number.

terms.definition: The record came from a densification pass. The pass number is dropped from the canonical tag and remains recoverable in tag_provenance.
The record was written to close a previously recorded round gap. The round and gap identifiers are dropped from the canonical tag and remain recoverable in tag_provenance.

facets.description: Structural links a tag encodes to another record.

terms.definition: The tag cross-references another record by id. The referenced id is dropped from the canonical tag and remains recoverable in tag_provenance.

facets.description: Free prose that the source corpus stored in a tag slot. The canonical tag records only that such a note existed; the prose itself stays in tag_provenance and is never interpreted.

terms.definition: The tag slot carried an identity note about how the two sides of a pair relate.

facets.description: Curation bookkeeping emitted by the transform itself, never read from a source tag.

terms.definition: At least one source tag in this container had no taxonomy mapping and was dropped from the canonical list. The dropped tags are listed in tag_provenance and in the transform's unmapped report.

pattern_rules.description: Matches round-gap closure markers such as 'post_r5_gap_closure', 'gap1-closure', and 'r4b_gap8_closed' after normalization. Labels that append further free text, such as 'r3b_gap6_closed_tables', deliberately do not match and stay unmapped.
Matches an 'identity_note: <prose>' tag slot after normalization.
